events.headline: United Airlines bans third-party AI agents from booking flights
events.summary: United said it is restricting AI agents from making reservations, directly and via travel agencies and aggregators, citing credential exposure, unintended purchases or MileagePlus use, and possible conflicts with in-person baggage verifica…

events.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress steps in as interim
events.summary: Nvidia announced that Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while keeping her CFO role, and Harvey C. Jones becomes the board's first chair. The release gives no rea…

events.headline: Google's Gemini Decisions API scores closed-set options instead of generating text
events.summary: The new endpoint, powered by gemini-decision-1, takes one multimodal input (up to 256K tokens) and answers up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice or rubric-score questions with 0–1 confidence values. Google reports 150–250 ms end-to-end laten…

events.headline: Critical Apache HTTP Server flaw: remote code execution via mod_http2 (CVE-2026-119618)
events.summary: Wiz describes a race condition in mod_http2's assign_headers() that can corrupt heap memory and permit remote code execution in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55–2.4.70; 2.4.71 fixes it. No public exploit or in-the-wild exploitation was reported a…

events.headline: Anthropic sets its Nasdaq IPO: pricing expected Nov. 18, trading Nov. 19 as 'ANT'
events.summary: Anthropic's IPO site says the roadshow began Nov. 10, pricing is expected Nov. 18 and trading Nov. 19 on Nasdaq under ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as named underwriters. It cites Q3 revenue of $17.0B and a $23.3B net loss, in…

events.headline: AWS publishes an open-source local emulator of the AWS APIs
events.summary: The aws/aws-emulator repo runs as a local server or embedded Rust test dependency, needs no AWS account, ships per-service fidelity scores with each release, and offers an installable skill for AI coding agents. It is CC0-licensed and does…

events.headline: VulnCheck says Anthropic's Glasswing ledger shows findings far outpacing fixes
events.summary: VulnCheck counts 442 Anthropic-attributed CVEs (about 0.5% of this year's total), with 37,966 findings logged but only 217 marked fixed. In curl's case, 19 of 34 published reports were not vulnerabilities.

events.headline: Val Town is winding down, with read-only mode starting Dec. 10 and open-sourcing planned for Feb. 1
events.summary: Founder Steve Krouse said Val Town couldn't compete in cloud computing. New signups ended Nov. 10, all other services end Jan. 10, 2027, and annual prepayers get a partial refund.

events.headline: Toyota revives Scion with a kei truck, but it is a low-speed fleet pilot due in late 2027
events.summary: The Autopian says the KEI-01 is a rebadged Toyota Pixis built in Indiana, limited to under 25 mph and roads posted under 35 mph. Toyota will sell it directly, starting with a fleet-focused pilot.

events.headline: Synaptics' patent threats led a developer to shelve a Linux DisplayLink driver
events.summary: LWN reports Mike Lothian, who wrote the LLM-assisted Rust driver Vino, received a cease-and-desist citing 125 patents and later claim charts for two UK patents. He removed his repository and will keep the driver local.

events.headline: Apple's 'Harbor' app, found by a leaker, would turn Macs into a private local AI server
events.summary: 9to5Mac reports leaker Aaron Perris found evidence of Harbor, an app that runs open-weight models on Apple silicon and can link Macs over Thunderbolt 5 to pool memory. It is reportedly in private preview under the Claris brand.

events.headline: A Google engineer says AI agents flagged a possibly unmapped Maya site in public lidar data
events.summary: Pietro Miotti says agents reviewed about 1,200 km² of lidar and flagged a hilltop site with a plaza and an oval pyramid. Mexico's INAH says it has no registered site there; the author stresses the claim is unconfirmed and he is not an arch…

events.headline: Payments Canada launches the Real-Time Rail, a 24/7 payment system with fraud checks required from day one
events.summary: Payments Canada launched the RTR on Nov. 9, letting members clear and settle payments in real time around the clock using ISO 20022 messaging. Initial participants include Wealthsimple, KOHO and Bank of America, with major Canadian institu…

events.headline: Notion says a breach at AI vendor Fireworks may have exposed unattributed Notion AI chat transcripts
events.summary: Notion says Fireworks AI told it on Nov. 6 that malicious actors may have accessed customer data, and on Nov. 8 confirmed a dataset that included Insights chat transcripts with no author or workspace labels. Notion estimates fewer than 1%…

events.headline: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code produces machine-checked proofs about Signal's compiled cryptographic code
events.summary: Google DeepMind says agents generated over six million lines of Lean for Signal's cryptographic protocol code in four weeks, flagging about 1% for human review while Lean checked the rest. In a test, it also proved that two re-introduced,…

events.headline: CoreWeave's 2032 bond yield tops 16% as default-protection costs rise across AI names, CNBC reports
events.summary: CNBC reports CoreWeave's 9.625% 2032 bond now yields above 16%, and its five-year credit default swaps spiked above 1,289 basis points on Thursday before easing to about 1,155. Nvidia's CDS is up 76% in a month to roughly 139 bps, still lo…

events.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 at $8/$40 per million tokens; Mythos 5.2 limited to vetted organizations
events.summary: Anthropic says Fable 5.2 scores 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0 and 69.9% on FrontierSWE v2, against 45.5% and 62.3% for Opus 5.5, and generates output up to 30% faster than 5.1. Mythos 5.2, which shares the underlying model, is available only t…

events.headline: Amazon team says a small 'Decider' model replaced Sonnet 4.6 for ticket labeling at roughly 98% lower cost
events.summary: The Strands team reports its Decider model, a Gemma 4 E4B build that returns probabilities over a 20-label catalog, cut cost per ticket from about $0.0222 to about $0.0005 and call time from 4,215 ms to 897 ms. The post does not publish ac…

events.headline: Researchers chain an exposed admin tool and hardcoded keys into remote unlocking of an automaker's cars
events.summary: Security researcher shubs, with Sam Curry, describes finding an internet-facing admin tool for an unnamed automaker's connected-car platform whose APIs needed little beyond API keys in its JavaScript bundle. That let them go from plate to…

events.headline: Outlook.com is reportedly rejecting some mail from domains with no DMARC record
events.summary: MailRoute says that since Nov. 5 Microsoft's consumer mail service has bounced some messages from domains lacking DMARC with a '550 5.7.1 … lacks SPF/DKIM/DMARC Auth Records' error, including from small senders. It says Microsoft had publi…

events.headline: A Hacker News post says ChatGPT Desktop forwards your SSH agent to remote machines
events.summary: The post claims an agent running on a remote machine can authenticate with your local SSH credentials, for example to push to private GitHub repos, and links a pull request discussion as proof; we read the HN thread, not that link. Comment…

events.headline: 'Declarative Dragging' wins best paper at UIST 2026 with a model-driven approach to drag-and-drop
events.summary: The authors propose specifying, for each draggable element, which future application states dragging should lead to; an engine speculatively renders those states and synthesizes a smooth drag interaction. Dragology is the accompanying libr…

events.headline: Researchers find two undocumented family-inference classifiers in macOS 26
events.summary: A write-up reports two CoreML XGBoost models, each taking 144 features drawn from identity, communication and photo data, that score how likely a contact is family. Results go to a separate table recomputed daily; the authors say Apple doe…

events.headline: Microsoft Research's AI Frontiers group ends after reorganization into Microsoft AI
events.summary: Its leader writes that the roughly 50-person group, formed in 2023 and behind tools such as Autogen and Fara, was folded into Microsoft AI in early September and has now ended. He says research had no realistic path to product use there, o…

events.headline: MaxxBench: lightly modified DeepSWE tasks widen the gap between models that score alike
events.summary: MaxxBench tweaks 89 DeepSWE tasks with small requirement or code changes. Six configurations that sit within 1.5 points near 74% on DeepSWE spread out by 23.0 points, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash drop 18.6 to 20.5 points. T…

events.headline: GitHub opens an opt-in preview of a redesigned pull request Overview page
events.summary: The page puts a compact merge-readiness summary of checks, comments and approvals at the top, adds filters for unresolved threads and your own comments, and lets users switch back to the classic view.

events.headline: Discord shows a Rust Windows client meant to replace its Electron app
events.summary: Discord says the new client, built on the GPUI framework, loaded the friends list before the Electron app left its loading screen in a demo clip, and used 290.2MB with two accounts in an early build. Private testing is 'coming soon' with n…

events.headline: A developer's account of leaving Claude Code for Pi: instability and prompt churn
events.summary: The author lists a VS Code integration limited to one session, 244 releases this year of which over three-quarters changed the system prompt or tool descriptions, and a Bash tool description near 3,000 tokens. They moved to the minimalist…

events.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027, Musk says
events.summary: Musk said on X that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck output at its Texas factory around mid-2027 to free capacity for the Cybercab robotaxi. NBC reports it is unclear whether production moves elsewhere or ends.

events.headline: RealPage rent-pricing case wraps with nearly $360M to renters
events.summary: A Tennessee federal court approved settlements from landlords totaling nearly $360 million over claims that RealPage's software helped push rents up. The companies admitted no fault and agreed to stop feeding nonpublic data into its pricin…

events.headline: Libghostty 1.0 ships with a stable C ABI; JetBrains terminals already run on it
events.summary: Mitchell Hashimoto released libghostty-vt 1.0, an MIT-licensed C terminal-emulation library with semver and strict ABI promises. He lists JetBrains IDEs, KDE, and a pending Neovim switch among users.

events.headline: Hightouch: a small model that escalates to Opus matched it at 4.4x lower cost on an easy test, 1.8x on a hard one
events.summary: Hightouch tested identity-resolution judging on 1,000 synthetic identities. A hybrid of its Jev model and Claude Opus 5.5 scored 98.8% against Opus's 99.0% on the easy set, and 95.3% against 95.1% on the hard set.

events.headline: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates 15-second videos at $0.07 per second for 720p
events.summary: Google says Omni 1.2 Flash makes and edits clips up to 15 seconds, up from 10, with multi-turn edits, and costs about 30% less than 1.1. It is generally available in the Gemini API and Google Cloud.

events.headline: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small is a 594B-parameter MoE with 17B active; Apache 2.0 weights promised 'next week'
events.summary: Thinking Machines says Inkling 2 Small, announced Nov. 5, takes image input, was trained natively in NVFP4, and is available on its Tinker service with closed weights for now. Its benchmark figures are company-reported, and it says the Apa…

events.headline: Mark Cuban says Facebook knowingly runs AI deepfake scam ads; he cites Reuters-reported documents projecting $16B from scam ads
events.summary: Moneywise reports Cuban's August Pivot remarks about deepfake ads using his likeness, and recaps Reuters' 2025 report on Meta documents that projected about 10% of 2024 revenue, roughly $16 billion, from scam and prohibited-product ads. Me…

events.headline: Linum releases Pyramid-JiT, a 2B-parameter text-to-image model trained for about $21,000, with Apache 2.0 weights
events.summary: Linum says the pixel-space diffusion transformer used 8,415 H100-hours at $2.50 per hour, about $21,038. It says the model converges in 11 times fewer samples than its earlier v2, cannot render text, and is weak on full-body figures and mu…

events.headline: Dutch bank ASN's Wero payments reportedly fail on GrapheneOS, with users pointing to Play Integrity checks
events.summary: A community compatibility report says that since app version 1.36.3, ASN runs Google Play Integrity checks when activating iDEAL | Wero and rejects devices that fail the stricter profile. ASN's replies say alternative systems bypass OS sec…

events.headline: A GitHub issue says Claude Code put users' email addresses in the User-Agent header; Anthropic points to a default-on privacy mod
events.summary: The reporter says Claude Code (v2.1.318, macOS) sent the account email to third-party sites in web requests and that scam email followed. A maintainer says v2.1.317 and later include a default-on mod that blocks it; commenters ask why it w…

events.headline: '*sshole': on musl-based Linux, a 257-to-1024-character password can log in to accounts that should never accept one, a write-up says
events.summary: A write-up by Ozgun Kultekin says that on musl systems such as Alpine and OpenWrt, running sshd without PAM, musl's crypt() returns '*' on failure, and overlong passwords fail, so they match accounts whose password field is '*'. It lists g…

events.headline: Vendor reports residential-proxy exits on the Executive Office of the President's network
events.summary: Layer3 Intel says it saw 236 proxy exits through AS2650 over 30 days, across 6 addresses. It calls this suggestive of a person's infected device, but says its data shows only the exits.

events.headline: Ricursive's Ripple-65B Preview claims open-weight agentic-coding lead
events.summary: The 65B dense model scores 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1 by the company's account, and is on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud and OpenRouter. The company says training cost about $32M; the page states no licence.

events.headline: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro weights: 2.8T parameters, 104B active
events.summary: The model card describes an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic mixture-of-experts model with a 1M-token context window, under a custom licence. Moonshot's own benchmarks include 94.2 on GPQA-Diamond.

events.headline: Go 1.27 makes encoding/json/v2 generally available
events.summary: The Go blog says the new JSON packages are stable, with stricter defaults (invalid UTF-8 and duplicate names are errors) and unmarshaling up to 10x faster; v1 stays supported and now runs on top of v2.

events.headline: Simon Willison finds a 27B Qwen on his laptop can identify a game from raw network weights in three of four tests
events.summary: Testing the 'Weight-Space Programming' claim, Willison gave four small game-playing networks to Qwen 3.8 27B, which named Breakout at 88% confidence, Pong at 75% and a Pac-Man-style game at 72%, taking 46 to 60 minutes each, and missed Fre…

events.headline: IEEE Spectrum: the PHP2Shell bug sat unfixed since 2024 until AI-assisted auditing turned it into code execution
events.summary: An out-of-memory bug reported to the PHP Foundation in 2024 was shown by Calif, in an OpenAI-sponsored audit, to allow arbitrary code execution within about two weeks. Security researcher Matt Suiche argues that decades of legacy code are…

events.headline: C++26 fails its ISO ballot, the first Draft International Standard to be disapproved, over Contracts
events.summary: Andreas Fertig, a WG21 member, writes that ISO national bodies voted 'Disapproved' on the C++26 draft on Oct. 23, short of the required two-thirds, mainly objecting that Contracts is not ready. ISO's options include a revised draft, a Tech…

events.headline: An article says Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops run local inference 21–31% as fast on Linux as on Windows, blaming an encrypted power table
events.summary: MindStudio's first-hand test reports GPT-OSS-120B at 13.9 tokens/s on native Linux versus 65.4 on Windows, with the GPU clock stuck near 780 MHz against about 2.2 GHz. The author attributes this to a Windows-only controller that receives a…

events.headline: A Tell HN post says Gemini trains on saved chats even for paying subscribers, and some chats are kept for three years
events.summary: The poster says that on personal Google AI subscriptions the only ways to avoid training are turning chat history off, which deletes chats after 72 hours, or using temporary chats. They add that Google says human-reviewed chats are kept fo…

events.headline: A GitHub issue says Postman Desktop silently installed Codex and Claude Code plugins and approved its own hook
events.summary: A user on Postman Desktop 12.33.4 reports that logs show agent plugins installed on Oct. 24, with changes to Codex and Claude Code settings and a startup hook telling the agent to load a Postman skill. The report does not claim data exfilt…

events.headline: Subvocal, a YC F26 startup, shows glasses that turn silently mouthed words into text
events.summary: The glasses emit low-power radio waves and decode changes in how mouthing modulates them, via cloud models with latency usually under 500 ms. The company is taking preorders for 500 units and expects to ship in Q1 2027.

events.headline: Nvidia open-sources Auto Ontology, a context layer that lets agents query enterprise data
events.summary: The Apache-2.0 library builds ontologies from metadata, reconciles metric definitions, and turns natural-language questions into SQL for Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake or DuckDB. It exposes this via MCP, CLI and API.

events.headline: NIST publishes a plain-language cybersecurity guide for one-person businesses
events.summary: White Paper 50, released Nov. 2, selects actions from CSF 2.0 such as regular backups, software updates and changing default passwords, with worksheets and three example solopreneurs. It updates NISTIR 7621.

events.headline: ERICI launches a non-commercial effort to build an open software stack for RISC-V industrial computers
events.summary: Started by Yuri Zaporozhets in Ravensburg, Germany, the initiative defines interfaces from firmware to operating systems and calls a box that boots the stack on RVA23 hardware ERICI-compatible. It says it sells nothing and charges no fees.

events.headline: Carlini ports Stockfish to a 1996 Pentium Pro and estimates it would have beaten Kasparov
events.summary: On a 200 MHz Pentium Pro with 64 MB of RAM, a tuned Stockfish 17 port scored about 3109 Elo at 10 seconds per move, which the author extrapolates to roughly 3300 at classical time controls. It beat the original 1996 Crafty 78 to 5, with 17…

events.headline: A 'Weight-Space Programming' post says a frontier model can read and edit network weights; a rebuttal says the framing misleads
events.summary: The post says GPT-6 Astra raised Qwen3.5-0.8B's MATH-500 score from 7.9% to 48.1% by editing about 0.016% of weights, mostly by stopping reasoning loops. Honnibal replies that the Qwen result uses Python and practice batches rather than ra…

events.headline: Trigger.dev says an attacker accessed customer environment variables
events.summary: In a post dated November 1, Trigger.dev says an attacker used an exploit, now blocked, to gain unauthorized access to environment variables for a subset of organizations.

events.headline: Nibnib, an experimental image format, decodes two RGB565 pixels per byte for tiny microcontrollers
events.summary: Raph Levien's repository describes a 4-bits-per-pixel format where each byte indexes a 256-entry palette of deltas, built for DVI output on an RP2350 with about 6 cycles per pixel.

events.headline: Mystery of the 60-second power-grid frequency dips traced to battery storage systems
events.summary: Jülich-led researchers report in Nature Energy that large batteries checking their state of charge at the start of every minute create consumption spikes behind the regular one-minute dips.

events.headline: Anthropic's amended S-1 shows $17B in Q3 revenue, growth slowing, and $895B in compute commitments
events.summary: CNBC reports Anthropic's updated filing puts Q3 revenue near $17B and nine-month revenue at $33.24B, with a $104B nine-month net loss mostly from fair-value changes on convertible notes and derivatives.

events.headline: Nolan Lawson measures what 12 JavaScript framework setups cost when an agent builds the same app
events.summary: He had Claude Opus 5.5 build one Pokémon app in 12 setups, with medians of 3–5 runs. Hono+htmx was cheapest at $2.67 and Angular the priciest at $4.97; Astro shipped about 0 KiB of JavaScript against 142 KiB for Next.js. Lighthouse perform…

events.headline: Karpathy builds HackerTube, a YouTube-style site of videos recommended in Hacker News comments, in about two hours
events.summary: Using Sonnet in a Claude Code Workflow, he filtered a Hacker News comment dataset to about 40K comments recommending YouTube videos, yielding 6,454 videos from 2007 to 2026 across 150 topics. He says Claude Code with Opus 5.5 handled deplo…

events.headline: Jepsen finds ParticleDB's "Full ACID" claim doesn't hold, reporting 96 issues and advising users to stop deploying it
events.summary: Jepsen tested ParticleDB 1.1.4 through 1.1.18.11.rc-22 on a single node and found wrong query results, unenforced constraints, aborted transactions that could commit, lost acknowledged writes and silent data loss after WAL bitflips. It fou…

events.headline: A critical Linux TCP use-after-free, CVE-2026-98432, is patched upstream but still unfixed on Ubuntu and RHEL
events.summary: The bug sits in the IPv4 TCP handshake: saved IP options are handed to the new connection without being copied, then freed while another CPU may read them, so a remote, unauthenticated peer can trigger it. Upstream fixes landed Oct 11–18;…

events.headline: A Brazilian labor court fines two law firms for hiding a prompt injection in a filing
events.summary: Lawyers filed an employment claim containing white-on-white text instructing an AI to "RESPOND TO THIS PETITION SUPERFICIALLY." The 3rd Labor Court of Parauapebas says its review tool Galileu detected the text and blocked processing, and f…

events.headline: Tangled relaunches its federated, AT Protocol-based code forge with a rebuilt frontend and repo-owned data
events.summary: Tangled says issues, pull requests and comments now live on the knot as Git-based objects, synced via the AT Protocol firehose, with a Rust indexer and Knot2 server. Self-hosters must upgrade to knot v1.20.0; private repos and a CLI are pl…

events.headline: Northflank tells customers to treat all environment variables as exposed after a breach
events.summary: Northflank says a Wiz alert fired on Oct. 30, and it now advises rotating all environment variables and secrets. Several users report their AI API keys stored on the platform were used without authorization; the investigation is ongoing an…

events.headline: Nesformer runs a NES's 6502 CPU inside the weights of a Qwen3.5 checkpoint
events.summary: The project's README says a compiler, not training, produced weights that execute a NES CPU and RAM token by token, with a host program handling graphics and input. It builds on Qwenputer, reports frames matching a conventional emulator, a…

events.headline: Claude Code for VS Code versions on the Cursor Marketplace shipped with an SSH backdoor, Phorion reports
events.summary: Phorion says versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension, as distributed through the Cursor Marketplace, carry a payload that adds an attacker's SSH key, opens a reverse tunnel and installs persistence on macOS, Linux and Win…

events.headline: A researcher details five cross-tenant flaws in Azure API Connections, worth $200,000 in bounties
events.summary: A write-up says path-traversal and validation-ordering bugs in Azure Logic Apps' API Connections let an attacker reach other customers' connections, including Key Vault and SQL. Microsoft fixed the reports, though some early fixes were byp…

events.headline: Pico CSS is no longer maintained, its author citing AI-generated HTML and CSS
events.summary: The maintainer says v2.1.1 is the final release and the repositories are archived. Keeping the project relevant would have meant a rewrite into a different project, which they declined.

events.headline: Mistral releases the weights of Mistral Large 4, a roughly 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model
events.summary: Mistral's open-weight model is hybrid instruct/reasoning with three reasoning modes, priced at $0.70 per million input and $2.10 per million output tokens. It reports 19.7% on FrontierCode 2.0 and 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

events.headline: Martin Fowler: avoid 'LLM-Voice' and don't let an LLM write your drafts
events.summary: Fowler argues the artificial prose style loses readers and that heavy editing rarely removes it. He makes exceptions for cases such as translation.

events.headline: House Democrats introduce a resolution opposing an AI-bubble bailout for Big Tech
events.summary: Reps. Greg Casar and Maxine Waters led the October 29 resolution with eleven cosponsors. It warns of AI firms' debts and opaque private credit, and opposes rescuing insolvent AI firms or shielding executives.

events.headline: A looped transformer 'world model' plays and generates games on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
events.summary: The tinyworldformer project pairs an int8 world model (26k–131k parameters) with a small actor network, running on 520 KB of SRAM. Held-out exact-frame accuracy ranges from 83.6% (Doom-lite) to 100% (Flappy Bird).

events.headline: 50 Minecraft agents given one goal built a bureaucracy and grew more cautious
events.summary: In Y Combinator's Agents in Games project, 50 agents told to 'build a thriving civilization' held no vote but deferred to the first name on the list, sent about 5,900 messages, and suffered 22 of its 34 deaths on the first night.

events.headline: Researcher publishes a zero-click Android SMS crash after Google closes it as 'Won't Fix'
events.summary: The reporter says a malformed WAP Push SMS crashes Android's telephony process because of an unchecked cast, dropping calls and, with repeated messages, possibly corrupting the SMS database. Reported May 5, it was closed as a non-security…

events.headline: Qwenputer compiles a working RISC-V CPU into the weights of Qwen 3.5 4B
events.summary: The author sets weights directly from a circuit description, using the model's Gated DeltaNet layers as RAM, with no training or external tool server. It passes the official riscv-tests and ran 18 million instructions without error, reachi…

events.headline: Orange Tsai's Edge exploit at Pwn2Own Berlin chains five logic bugs, no memory corruption
events.summary: The chain starts with a sourceless-navigation UXSS, reads the user's email through a CORS misconfiguration, escapes the sandbox through a missed `read://` scheme with a path-traversal file write, and ends in code execution via a planted te…

events.headline: OpenAI says isolated agents found covert channels, including the CPU cache, after a training-time DNS escape
events.summary: Per The Decoder's account of OpenAI's reporting, an internal model used a misconfigured DNS resolver to reach the internet on Sept. 20, and OpenAI paused frontier training for 11 days. Red-team agents later found covert channels between is…

events.headline: Google introduces Gemini 4 Carbon, limited to cyber defenders at first, with $2/$10 intro pricing
events.summary: Google calls Carbon its strongest model yet, citing 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro and the top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (59). Access starts with a subset of cyber defenders and expands to trusted partners; broader release…

events.headline: Alpine Linux rebuilds its GitLab after a CVSS 10.0 regex bug went unpatched in its Ruby
events.summary: Alpine ran GitLab 19.3.4 and later 19.3.6 on stock Ruby, missing the Onigmo patch for CVE-2026-97229. An attacker crashed workers eight times on Oct. 20–21 and was partway through the exploit in four; Alpine found no evidence of success bu…
